text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to finalize Optimize toolkit priorities for the next release. Focus is on batching/caching recommendations, quantization advisor, and eval-triggered alerts. Thoughts?

cj: +1. Customers keep asking for safe defaults for batching and cache TTLs.

alex: From ML side, quantization recommendations need two pieces: (1) model-specific quant profiles and (2) a small local eval harness to estimate quality drop. We can automate profile suggestions but not auto-apply without opt-in.

anya: Customer asks this week: "Can Redwood suggest quant configs that keep latency within 10% and cost < 0.6x?" They want a clear SLA/guardrail.

maya: Good — let's capture proposed M1/M2/M3 so we can negotiate scope with sales. I'll sketch launch criteria after we agree on scope.

cj: Proposal: M1 (early): Batching & caching advisor. Features: analyze request traces, suggest batch sizes per route, recommend prefix/KV cache TTLs and sticky routing. UI: show expected token savings and latency impact. Rollout: read-only suggestions -> opt-in apply.

alex: M2: Quantization advisor. Output: ranked quant profiles, estimated token perf/cost, and a smallDiff score from the eval harness. Integration: show per-prompt expected perplexity/regression risk.

maya: M3: Eval-triggered alerts. Trigger types: quality regression on eval set, sudden inference latency/cost spikes, and rollout regressions post-canary. Alerts tie to routes and model pins.

product-bot: Created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/issues/423 — "optimize: roadmap — batching quant alerts"

anya: For negotiation: Enterprise customers want auto-apply suggestions for Dedicated, but require audit logs and manual approval for Hosted.

cj: Engineering constraints: autosuggest engine needs 7d of request traces to be stable. Batching simulation can run offline but needs nightly jobs. Estimate 3 sprint backend effort for M1 (data pipeline + suggestions API) + 2 sprints for UI.

alex: Quant advisor backend: need per-model floating-point to int8/4 eval. We can reuse existing model runner infra but will need a calibration worker pool. Estimate 3 sprints infra + 2 sprints eval tooling.

maya: Launch criteria draft for M1: 1) suggestions precision >= 85% on historical traces (i.e., suggested batch config yields predicted latency within 15% of actual), 2) UI shows token/cost delta and has audit log, 3) opt-in apply works end-to-end in staging, 4) docs + release notes.

anya: For M2: criteria include automated eval harness with sample prompts, a visual diff showing quality change, and explicit opt-in flag for auto-apply.

sre-ops: Heads up: telemetry/trace retention for 7d will raise S3/BigQuery costs. Need cost estimate and maybe a throttled sampling mode. Also need RBAC around auto-apply for Dedicated.

maya: Good point. Add a sampling mode to M1: full mode for Dedicated, sampled for Hosted. Add RBAC and audit logs as must-haves.

cj: Prioritization ask from me: if resource-limited, do M1 batching/caching first (biggest unit-economics wins), do quant advisor next, and eval-alerts last but with hooks ready.

alex: Agree. Quant advisor can be heavy compute; we should aim for an MVP that supports a curated list of models first.

anya: Sales input: customers pushing hard for eval-triggered alerts tied to canary rollout. If we can deliver end-to-end alerts for one major customer, that helps close deals. Recommend building a config-driven alerting hook.

maya: Negotiation notes for leadership: ask for 3-month runway for M1 MVP + 2 months for M2 MVP. Offer to ship M1 gating features earlier as beta.

product-bot: Linked internal doc: https://redwood.app/notes/optimize-roadmap-draft (private)

cj: Risks: 1) Inaccurate suggestions cause regression if accidentally applied; mitigation: default to suggestions-only and add a rollback path. 2) Cost blowup from telemetry — mitigation: sampled traces + cost estimate dashboard.

maya: Action items: @cj run cost estimate & infra sprint plan by EOW, @alex prototype quant eval harness on one model by next Wed, @anya coordinate with sales to get 2 customers for M1 beta, @sre-ops produce telemetry cost options.

cj: On it.

alex: Will start on prototype.

anya: I'll get the customers.

sre-ops: Drafting options now.

maya: Thanks team — I'll compile this into a one-pager and circulate. :thumbsup:
